3 · Place, reject, and undo

Why undo even after finding a solution? Choose n=4 and advance one event at a time: × is a rejected square, Q is a placed queen, and ? marks the square just undone. Rows increase downward and columns rightward, both from 0. Inspect the board and sets, then the previous event; completed boards remain in the ledger below. Find an undo, step back, and forward again to verify that both sets and saved results are restored.

Invariant: at entry to search(r), placement records exactly the legal columns of the first r rows; the three sets contain exactly their c, r−c, and r+c keys. Backtracking means removing that choice and all three keys after exploring it, restoring the state before trying the next column.

This is a deterministic JavaScript teaching simulation of the Python algorithm, not Python execution in the browser. Every event for n=1…4 is retained with no skipped search. Larger factorial searches do not run in the UI. Snapshot memory is separate from submission space.

2 · Use the last character or skip it?

Which two new ways does the last a add to aaa → aa? A prefix is the beginning of a string. Let D(i,j) count position choices from the first i source characters spelling the first j target characters. Table rows are i and columns are j; ∅ denotes an empty prefix.

Skip position 2: only (0,1) remains, giving D(2,2)=1. Use position 2: it matches the final target a, so we need a single a before it. Choices (0) and (1) give D(2,1)=2 ways; appending position 2 yields (0,2) and (1,2). The two groups are disjoint and cover every way, so 3=1+2.

If the last characters differ, as b and a do in ab → aa, we cannot use that b as the target’s last letter. Only skipping is allowed, so the count stays 0. If they match, each shorter-target choice extends uniquely by the current source position.

D(i,j) = D(i−1,j) + (s[i−1] = t[j−1] ? D(i−1,j−1) : 0)

Why these boundaries? There is exactly one way to form an empty target: skip everything. Thus D(i,0)=1. An empty source cannot spell a nonempty target, so D(0,j)=0 for j>0. For aaa → aa the rows are [1,0,0], [1,1,0], [1,2,1], and [1,3,3].
